 Appearance:

sentences.text: 2. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that in present case, the investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
The offences alleged against the present applicant are triable by the Court of Magistrate.
The applicant herein has not played any significant role in commission of the offence in question.
The other co-accused have been considered for grant of bail by this Court, and therefore, the applicant is also entitled to be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.

He, therefore,
submitted to allow the present application and enlarge the present applicant on bail subject to suitable conditions.

sentences.text: 1 3. Learned APP has opposed the present application, inter alia, contending that the applicant had actively participated in commission of the offence in question, as he along with other co- accused were actively involved in hatching a conspiracy for commission of the offence in question and had also acted in furtherance of the said conspiracy.
He, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present application.
4. Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the material available on record.

As per the case of prosecution, the husband of the first informant had received a phone call on his mobile phone and he was informed that the person on the other side was a Customs Officer and he was calling from Delhi.

He was further informed that the parcel, which had been dispatched by the husband of the first informant to Cambodia had been intercepted and an offence in that regard had been registered against him at Vasantvihar Police Station, Delhi.
Thereafter, he was threatened of involving him in a serious offence and he was made to deposit huge sum of Rs.1,40,00,000/- in the different accounts, as directed by those persons.
In fact, the person, who had called the husband of the first informant, was not a Customs Officer and thus, it was a fraud call made to the husband of the first informant.

The husband of the first informant was shown fake identity cards of police officials and CBI Officers and was threatened that he would be booked for an offence of money laundering and a huge sum had been demanded from him.

The role attributed to the present applicant in commission of the offence is to the effect that he got a bank account opened in the name of co-accused Rahul Rajesh Jangid NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22877/2024 ORDER DATED:
12/12/2024 undefined with IndusInd Bank and out of the amount of Rs.90 lacs which the husband of the first informant had transferred, the amount of Rs.4 lacs had been transferred to the said account through Net Banking by the present applicant.

Having regard to the material available on record, it can be prima facie said that the present applicant was actively involved in the offence since its inception and the applicant was also part of a group, which were hatched a conspiracy for commission of the present offence.
The other co-accused, who had been considered for grant of bail were attributed a role, which was different than the role attributed to the present applicant.
Those co-accused were alleged to have provided their bank accounts to the other co-accused for being used in commission of the offence.

Except this, no other overt act had been attributed to them nor they have received any monetary gain out of the same except some commission, whereas the present applicant, as stated herein above, had got a bank account opened in the name of other co-accused and had also transferred money to the said bank account.
Therefore, the applicant cannot claim parity with the other co-accused, who have been considered for grant of bail.
Hence, the present application stands dismissed.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) GIRISH Surendrabhai Pintubhai Chauhan vs State Of Gujarat on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41110799/
